newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Sumitomo Finance refocuses in London.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Sumitomo Finance refocuses in London.

text.p: Sumitomo Finance International, the capital markets subsidiary of Japan's Sumitomo Bank, said on Tuesday it had axed 10 fixed income staff in London as part of a refocusing of the business towards more niche areas.
The decision follows similar end-of-year changes by other firms.

Earlier this month Swiss banking giant Credit Suisse cut around 30 jobs from its foreign exchange and treasury operations in London, while First Chicago NBD Corp said it will close its U.S. Treasuries trading operation early next year, making five people redundant in London.
Sumitomo Bank is part of the same group as Sumitomo Corp, but the bank has not been involved in the scandal surrounding Sumitomo Corp's copper trader Yasuo Hamanaka.
Sumitomo Finance's head of operations Roger Preece told Reuters the 10 staff members going were involved in European government bond trading and sales.
He said the changes were being made because Sumitomo was shifting the emphasis of its business away from this area, although it would continue to quote prices to clients who wanted this service
